questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The current distribution of goods between two individuals in a two-person economy with given technology and resources is at point X. According to the Pareto criterion, which point would definitely indicate increased allocative efficiency? A Tariq’s goods X B C D O Samir’s goods

The concept of allocative efficiency assumes that each individual in society is the best judge of their own economic welfare. Which example of government intervention is based on an argument which rejects this assumption?

options.A: pollution controls
options.B: subsidies for merit goods
options.C: the provision of public goods
options.D: the regulation of monopolies

questions.questionText: In the indifference curve diagram point M is the consumer’s initial equilibrium and MN is the substitution effect of a fall in the price of good X. If good X is a Giffen good which point will be the consumer’s new equilibrium point after the fall in the price of good X? J A B C good Y D M N I O K L good X
To maximise the satisfaction he derives from a given level of expenditure on two goods, X and Y, a consumer should allocate his expenditure between the two goods so that

options.A: marginal utility of X = price of X and marginal utility of Y = price of Y.
options.B: marginal utility of X plus marginal utility of Y is maximised.
options.C: marginal utility of X = marginal utility of Y. marginal utility of X price of X
options.D: = price of Y. marginal utility of Y

questions.questionText: Which statement about the ‘kinked demand curve’ model of oligopoly is incorrect?

options.A: The kink in the demand curve of each firm is based on expectations about other firms’ responses to changes in its price.
options.B: The marginal revenue curve of the firm has a vertical segment at the market price.
options.C: The model explains how the equilibrium market price is determined.
options.D: The model suggests price stickiness within a certain range of marginal costs.

questions.questionText: A monopolist changes its objective from profit maximisation to sales revenue maximisation. MC H AC P cost, revenue P J K G F L AR MR O Q Q
A firm estimates that, all else remaining unchanged, an increase in its output will result in a fall in its revenue. What can be concluded from this?

options.A: The demand for the firm’s product is price-elastic.
options.B: The demand for the firm’s product is price-inelastic.
options.C: The supply of the firm’s product is price-elastic.
options.D: The supply of the firm’s product is price-inelastic.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the cost and revenue curves of a firm. MC ATC cost, revenue D MR O quantity What does the diagram represent?

options.A: a firm in monopolistic competition making normal profit
options.B: a firm in monopolistic competition making short-term losses
options.C: a firm in perfect competition at long-run equilibrium
options.D: a monopoly making abnormal profits

questions.questionText: Which is a risk-bearing economy of scale?

options.A: greater bargaining power in purchasing from suppliers
options.B: greater diversification of the product range
options.C: lower costs in raising capital
options.D: lower distribution costs by increasing market share

questions.questionText: A firm wishes to eliminate competition and become a monopoly. What should it do?

options.A: maximise output
options.B: maximise profit
options.C: reduce prices
options.D: reduce the number of its suppliers

questions.questionText: In many developed economies, clothes are designed by small firms and retailed by large firms. What is the most likely explanation for this pattern? clothes design firms clothes retail firms

options.A: need to be flexible to cope need to exploit marketing with frequent fashion changes economies of scale
options.B: need to employ highly need to operate at a low specialised and skilled workers minimum efficient scale
options.C: need to operate at a high need to offer a wide range minimum efficient scale of products to survive
options.D: need to overcome high need to take advantage of barriers to entry into the industry technical economies of scale

questions.questionText: What is likely to have its cause in the separation of ownership and control in a firm?

options.A: contestable markets
options.B: diseconomies of scale
options.C: principal-agent problem
options.D: prisoner’s dilemma

questions.questionText: A firm employs a worker who adds less to output than the previous worker employed. What does this illustrate?

options.A: decreasing marginal costs
options.B: diseconomies of scale
options.C: increasing returns to scale
options.D: the law of diminishing returns

questions.questionText: To increase the number of cleaners at a local school from 10 to 11, the employer has to raise the hourly rate of pay from $8.00 to $8.50. What is the marginal cost of labour per hour to the employer?
For a firm in imperfect competition, the marginal revenue product of labour at any given level of employment is equal to

options.A: marginal revenue divided by the number employed.
options.B: marginal revenue divided by the wage rate.
options.C: the marginal physical product of labour multiplied by marginal revenue.
options.D: the marginal physical product of labour multiplied by the wage rate.

questions.questionText: Which policy would be most effective in achieving a more equal distribution of disposable incomes between households?

options.A: government support for trade unions
options.B: import duties on manufactured goods
options.C: minimum wage policy
options.D: progressive income taxes

questions.questionText: A government regulates the price charged by a monopolist. In which circumstance will such intervention improve economic efficiency?

options.A: The government sets the price where average revenue equals marginal cost.
options.B: The government sets the price where marginal cost is below average cost.
options.C: The intervention results in an increase in producer surplus.
options.D: The intervention results in predatory pricing.

questions.questionText: What would cause estimates of the money value of the ‘Measure of Economic Welfare’ for a country to be greater than the value of ‘Gross National Product’?

options.A: negative externalities such as pollution
options.B: property income received from abroad
options.C: regrettable necessities
options.D: the value of non-marketed activities and leisure

questions.questionText: In 2012 a United Nations report calculated the stock of wealth of 20 countries in terms of human, natural and produced resources. This was measured as the Inclusive Wealth Index (IWI). The diagram shows the annual percentage (%) change in the IWI between 1990 and 2008 of the economies with the fastest and the slowest growth in IWI. It also shows their 2008 GDP per head ($). change in inclusive wealth index, 1990-2008 key GDP human China 3404 natural Kenya 722 produced Nigeria 1401 inclusive Russia 11 704 wealth index –25 0 25 50 75 % What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: A low level of GDP per head meant an inability to build stocks of wealth.
options.B: No country was able to prevent depletion of its natural resources.
options.C: The faster the growth in a country’s IWI the higher was its GDP.
options.D: There was an increase in human resources in all four countries.

questions.questionText: Which combination is usually found in less developed economies? low high

options.A: capital:output ratio saving ratio
options.B: external debt capital:output ratio
options.C: population growth external debt
options.D: saving ratio population growth

questions.questionText: Which change is most likely to increase both economic growth and economic development in the long run?

options.A: a decrease in the saving ratio
options.B: an increase in investment in human capital
options.C: the depletion of non-renewable resources
options.D: the greater use of compulsory overtime working of labour

questions.questionText: Which type of unemployment occurs when aggregate demand is deficient?

options.A: cyclical unemployment
options.B: regional unemployment
options.C: seasonal unemployment
options.D: structural unemployment

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the annual percentage (%) change in employment and output in the UK private sector between 2000 and 2012.
According to Keynesian theory, when will an increase in the money supply leave the level of output unchanged?

options.A: when the liquidity trap is operative
options.B: when the money supply increase was not anticipated
options.C: when there is a floating exchange rate
options.D: when there is an immediate adjustment to expectations about future price levels

questions.questionText: In a 4-sector economy, consisting of households, firms, government and foreign trade, the level of national income is in equilibrium where

options.C: S + T
options.A: C + S + M
options.B: C + S + T
options.D: S + T + M

questions.questionText: When would an economic recession result in an increase in a government’s budget deficit?

options.A: The government increases tariffs on imports with inelastic demand and keeps the total amount it spends on unemployment benefit unchanged.
options.B: The government keeps the unemployment benefit rate and direct and indirect tax rates unchanged.
options.C: The government reduces foreign aid and widens the tax base.
options.D: The government reduces the unemployment benefit rate and decreases the tax free allowance on income tax.

questions.questionText: What will be most likely to rise if unemployment is increasing in an economy?

options.A: the human capital of unemployed workers
options.B: the living standards of all workers
options.C: the nominal money wage rate of employed workers
options.D: the tax burden on employed workers

questions.questionText: What is most likely to result from foreign direct investment in developing economies?

options.A: a deterioration in the trade balances of developing economies
options.B: a reduction in migration to urban areas in developing economies
options.C: a reduction in the transfer of technology to developing economies
options.D: a rise in per capita levels of consumption in developing economies

questions.questionText: What will increase the multiplier effect of an increase in government spending on national income?

options.A: an increase in direct taxation
options.B: an increase in interest rates
options.C: an increase in the marginal propensity to consume
